messages:
maya: FYI customer 'BrightLane' reporting p99 latency jump on /v1/generate since ~2026-03-14T03:12Z. p95 looks OK but p99 went from ~600ms -> 2.4s. They attached a few traces.
omar: ugh. any config changes rolled?
jules: no infra deploys in that window, only a config push to continuous-batcher defaults on 03:10Z (auto-rollout).
maya: tagging the rollout: config-service change id cfg-9842. It increased default max_batch_size from 64 -> 128 and idle_timeout_ms from 8 -> 20.
liam: that would make sense. Bigger batches + longer idle means small-request workloads can get starved waiting for batch fill. p95 stable because common cases fill fast, p99 spikes when a tail request misses batch and waits.
maya: BrightLane says their profile is lots of short prompts (avg tokens ~12) and occasional long ones.
omar: can we reproduce? I'll try a synthetic load that mirrors their pattern: many concurrent tiny requests with occasional long ones.
ojames: (typo - actually jules) attaching a quick repro curl script: 
```
# hammer short prompts, occasional long
for i in $(seq 1 800); do
  if (( i % 50 == 0 )); then
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/run -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"input":"long prompt ... 2048 tokens"}' &
  else
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/run -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"input":"short"}' &
  fi
done
wait
```
maya: logs from one affected worker (trimmed):
```
2026-03-14T03:13:02Z worker-12 batcher: scheduling batch id=315 size=2 max=128 wait_ms=1900
2026-03-14T03:13:02Z worker-12 batcher: batch id=315 flush(reason=idle_timeout) latency=2200ms
2026-03-14T03:13:02Z worker-12 serve: req=abc123 p99=2245ms
```
liam: batches of 2 with a 20ms (or 2000ms?) wait recorded — the log's wait_ms looks like ms but shows 1900 which matches the new idle_timeout 20 (weird units?). Need to double-check units.
jules: config file snippet that went out: 
```
continuous_batcher:
  default_max_batch: 128
  idle_wait_ms: 2000   # intended 2s (misread), previous was 8 (ms?)
  adaptive_threshold_pct: 0.75
```
maya: oh. looks like the previous values were in microseconds in comments and someone misinterpreted. The net effect: idle wait jumped to 2s for small batches. That directly explains 2s p99.
omar: immediate mitigation: rollback to previous config and/or reduce idle_wait_ms to 8 (or 8ms?) and cap default_max_batch back to 64. Which one less risky?
liam: safe path: update idle_wait_ms -> 50ms and default_max_batch -> 64, push as hotfix to config-service. That reduces tail while we evaluate batching heuristics.
maya: I'll open a config rollback. Creating ticket SRE-1489 and patch cfg-9842-rollback.
(Infra-bot): deploy-plan: config-service patch cfg-9842-rollback created, target is all regions, canary in us-west-2.
jules: also suggest per-model batch caps for chatty models; put a short-term rule: if avg_tokens < 32 -> max_batch 32 and idle_wait_ms 40ms.
liam: agree. Also enable 'immediate_flush' flag for requests with 'low_latency': true header clients can set. BrightLane can try this.
maya: reaching out to BrightLane support now with repro request and temporary headers. @support-bot can you send the Kannary support snippet?
support-bot: sent DM template to support rep Sid.
omar: small follow-up: we should check whether KV-cache warmups for long requests are being blocked by large batches (e.g., when long request arrives, the batcher waits and then flushes combining long+short causing the long request's decoding to block). Look at per-request scheduling logs.
jules: correct — logs show some long requests got into mixed batches, and their total completion time was also high. We should add a rule to not co-batch short+long beyond a token delta threshold.
liam: notes for postmortem: root cause = mistaken units + aggressive batch size increase; contributing = lack of per-workload heuristics for short prompt heavy customers, and rollout lacked canary on batch-sensitive config.
maya: action items:
- maya: rollback patch (in progress) -> ETA 5m
- jules: prepare canary config with conservative defaults + per-token rules -> ETA 30m
- omar: run repro harness and post p95/p99 before/after -> ETA 20m
- liam: add immediate_flush flag and document usage -> ETA 2h (low priority)
- support: notify BrightLane & provide workaround header

maya: BrightLane responded: they can toggle low_latency header client-side for now. They appreciated quick response :thumbsup:
omar: after rollback (03:18Z) we see p99 drop to ~630ms in us-west-2 canary, will monitor global roll.
(Infra-bot): cfg-9842-rollback applied to us-west-2 canary at 03:18:22Z
maya: keeping this thread open until global roll and 24h monitoring. Will add postmortem link later.
liam: small follow: let's add a validation check in config-service to reject idle_wait_ms > 500ms unless explicitly acknowledged for specific models. Saves us from unit confusion next time.
jules: I'll file CONFIG-VALIDATION ticket.
maya: thanks all. closing in once global confirmed. :white_check_mark:
